newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Indonesia palm olein stable in late trade.
newsitem.headline: Indonesia palm olein stable in late trade.

text.p: Indonesian palm olein prices were mostly stable in late trading on Thursday with buyers showing scant interest, traders said.
They said olein was quoted at 1,435-40 rupiah/kg in Jakarta, unchanged from the opening, but buyers were eyeing 1,430 rupiah. Crude palm oil was last done at 1,250 rupiah/kg.
The traders said the market was subdued because of the Moslem Ramadan fasting month, and prices were under pressure from intervention selling by state logistics agency BULOG.
They said BULOG was continuing to sell olein at 1,435 rupiah/kg, aiming to put a lid on cooking oil prices.
"The market was quiet because of Ramadan," one trader said. "BULOG selling is putting pressure on prices."
But another trader said he expected prices to improve next week as consumer demand rises as Eid al-Fitr, the culmination of the Ramadan month, draws closer.
"BULOG is trying to keep prices low, but other sellers are still offering at slightly above BULOG levels because they feel prices will improve next week," one trader said.
Another trader said the relatively high price of crude palm oil was keeping olein margins in negative territory.
"At current crude palm oil prices there's no margin in olein," one trader said. "We will be making losses if we sell olein at 1,435 rupiah."
Data from Belawan Port showed the MT Ventura will leave for Port Klang with 11,390 tonnes of crude palm oil on Saturday.
The MT Bunga Tanjung will leave the North Sumatran port on Friday for Batam with 5,000 tonnes of crude palm oil.
The MV Bun Dong will leave for Port Klang, Malaysia with 6,000 tonnes of palm kernel oil on Friday. The KM Permanem will leave for Semarang on Friday with 1,800 tonnes of palm olein.
